title: The wool mills of Doire ghlas go over to holdout coal
summary: Tional nan Tuathach's wool mills at Doire ghlas sign to take their winter coal from Cnoc thais and Muileann àrsaidh rather than Comhairle nam Mèinnean's yard at Cathair mhòr, Comhairle nam Mèinnean's price having risen twice in two years. A clerk at Cathair mhòr, sorting another's tray, is the first at Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own table to read the contract.

title: A brewer of Baile ìseal writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean unasked
summary: A brewer of Baile ìseal writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean that he sees no shame in buying whichever coal comes cheapest, and will take no lecture from a Board that has never once carried coal north of the boundary stones for a Tuathach hearth to burn. The letter is filed and not answered.

title: Fearghas mac Aonghais calls for the northern returns
summary: The master of Comhairle nam Mèinnean calls for the northern returns drawn town by town, a thing he has not asked of his clerk in four years. Seumas mac Eachainn spends the better part of a day setting the wool mills' new contract against the year before and finds no part of the fall lying anywhere but in the five holdout towns' own trade.

title: Breith Leòid read again at Cathair mhòr
summary: Seumas mac Eachainn carries Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own copy of Breith Leòid to the master's room and hears it read through: that a right to work a seam fails with the fifth, whatever the reason the fifth stopped coming in. Fearghas mac Aonghais finds in it no clause that asks whether Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own reason for ceasing to carry the coal was a fair one.

title: Seumas mac Eachainn's report leaves out the carrying
summary: Writing the master's report by lamplight, Seumas mac Eachainn sets down every figure he has checked twice and is true, and leaves out, because the master did not ask for it, that Comhairle nam Mèinnean stopped carrying the western pits' coal four years before the pits stopped paying the fifth for it.

title: The shutting order carried north to the maor
summary: Comhairle nam Mèinnean's courier brings the sealed order to the maor of the western Seann Skell, who reads it standing at his own door and sends for the town's clerk as a second witness before the ink is a day old, judging rightly that the western towns will not obey a paper.

title: The five towns' unsigned answer
summary: Word of the shutting order passes hand to hand among Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais and Àth leathan, and an answer goes back to no one in particular: that the pits stopped paying the fifth the day Comhairle nam Mèinnean stopped carrying their coal, and will pay it again the day the carrying starts. It never reaches Comhairle nam Mèinnean as a formal reply.

title: The five towns meet at Muileann àrsaidh again
summary: Ruth Calder reads Comhairle nam Mèinnean's order aloud in the pit-shed at Muileann àrsaidh, twice through. Tom Varley wants it answered clause for clause; Ruth holds that the only answer that matters is whether coal comes up the morning after the order's date. It does, and the towns vote to go on as before.

title: Somhairle mac Lachlainn given the western command
summary: Called before Fearghas mac Aonghais and a councillor of the Rìoghachd, Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given command of forty of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's enforcers, to hold the shutting order at the five pit-heads and to close no house, road or town beyond them. He is told plainly that his business is to hold the order, not to fight a war nobody has declared.

title: Somhairle mac Lachlainn rides the road ahead of his company
summary: Two days ahead of his forty men, Somhairle mac Lachlainn rides alone across the boundary stones to see the ground he must hold, and lodges a night short of the western Seann Skell turning over, for the first time in eighteen years of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's service, whether a smuggler's quay and a country under a shutting order are the same kind of work.

title: The company quartered above the harbour
summary: Forty of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's enforcers come up the coast road to the western Seann Skell in a day's rain and are watched into the town without a stone thrown or a word of welcome. Somhairle mac Lachlainn quarters them in the old customs shed and pays the maor's clerk for its use out of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own purse rather than requisition it.

title: Tom Varley gives the posted men their tea
summary: Two of Somhairle's men are sent to stand at the pit-head of Cnoc thais with the shutting order nailed to the winding-gear. Tom Varley reads it without a word, tells them they are welcome to stand there as long as they like, and sees them given tea at midday like anyone else standing about in the wet. The coal comes up all the same.

title: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh notes the first company since An Dealachadh
summary: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh sets down the company's quartering in a few plain lines and adds, in her own hand, that it is the first the kingdom has sent armed toward the north since An Dealachadh itself, ninety years gone, and that no one now living who signed the truce is left to say whether it can stay a policing matter.

title: The margins of Breith Leòid
summary: Comhairle nam Mèinnean's press copy of Breith Leòid carries in its margins the circuit rulings that settled it: that a holder's right runs with An Crùn's fifth, and that nothing binds Comhairle nam Mèinnean to carry any holder's coal.

title: Forty men chosen for the western company
summary: Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given forty of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's enforcers for the western Seann Skell and chooses men who have served under him before.

title: The order nailed to the winding-gear
summary: The western company posts two men at each pit-head of the five towns with Comhairle nam Mèinnean's order nailed to the winding-gear, to report twice weekly whether coal comes up. It comes up.

title: The granary factors of Achadh mhòr
summary: The granary factors of Achadh mhòr sell a winter's oats to the pit towns of the western hills through Tional nan Tuathach's granaries, and write to Comhairle nam Mèinnean that they know of no rule against it.

title: The Brìde house of Caol ruadh burns its last stored coal
summary: The house of Brìde at Caol ruadh burns the last of the altar coal it stored in the undercroft, and its custodians write to the Àrd-choimheadaiche asking where the next is to come from.
